points.description: Argues that at steady state all derivatives vanish, including the integrator state (ξ̇ = r − θ = 0), so θ = r exactly, independent of a, b and c (ξ just settles at whatever value supplies the needed control; only requires stability, and b ≠ 0). A bare statement 'integral action removes error' without the ξ̇ = r − θ = 0 argument earns nothing.

Names one valid practical failure mode of integral action AND gives its matching standard remedy. Acceptable pairs: integrator windup with saturation – anti-windup (clamping/conditional integration/back-calculation); reduced stability margin/phase lag – lower KI or place integral pole slower, etc.; integration of sensor bias – calibration or leaky integrator. Failure mode without a matching remedy (or vice versa) earns no mark.

rubric.notes: P1: full mark for the ξ̇ = 0 ⇒ θ = r argument showing independence from b and c. P2: full mark for one valid failure mode paired with a correct remedy; no mark if only one of the two is given or they do not match. Marks are whole numbers only.
